title: Shadow scoring/ingestion: backpressure + circuit breaker (fail-open) with SRE metrics
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes:
- Shadow scoring/ingestion now degrades safely under backlog (drops shadow work first, never user path)
- New metrics for queue lag, drops, breaker state; default alert rules added to internal alert pack
body:
## Context
During internal dogfood we saw two correlated issues:
1) When scoring workers fall behind (GPU/CPU contention), the scoring queue lag grows and we keep accepting mirrored events at the same rate.
2) When ingestion is degraded (consumer lag / downstream write slowness), we amplify pressure by continuing to emit high-volume shadow artifacts.

This PR adds explicit backpressure + circuit breaker behavior for the shadow pipeline. Importantly: the user/control path must remain unaffected (fail-open).

## What this changes
### 1) Backpressure at the scoring enqueue boundary
- Adds a bounded in-memory admission controller in `shadow-score-dispatcher` (per-tenant + global):
  - `max_in_flight` semaphore for scoring jobs
  - overflow behavior: drop shadow scoring job + emit `dropped_reason` metric/event
  - optional sampling downshift (progressive) when we are near capacity
- Adds dedupe for (request_fingerprint, rubric_version, shadow_variant) within a short TTL to avoid re-scoring duplicate traffic during retry storms.

### 2) Circuit breaker when ingestion/scoring is unhealthy
- Adds a circuit breaker to the shadow artifact emit path (telemetry producer):
  - Opens when either:
    - scoring queue lag exceeds threshold (based on queue depth + moving average service rate), OR
    - ingestion consumer lag exceeds threshold (Kafka consumer lag proxy), OR
    - downstream write error rate > threshold over rolling window
  - When open:
    - routing continues to execute control request normally
    - shadow mirroring remains enabled at policy level, but artifacts are not emitted (effectively: shadow disabled) until breaker half-opens
  - Half-open: allow 1% of shadow events for 60s; close on success, reopen on lag regression.
- All breaker state changes are rate-limited and written to audit-ish operational logs (not customer-visible audit log; that’s separate work).

### 3) SRE-requested metrics (+ default alerts for internal tenants)
New metrics (all cardinality-safe; tenant is bucketed for internal only):
- `shadow_scoring_queue_lag_seconds{env,region}` (gauge)
- `shadow_scoring_admission_in_flight{env,region}` (gauge)
- `shadow_scoring_admission_dropped_total{env,region,reason}` (counter; reason is enum)
- `shadow_ingest_consumer_lag{env,region,topic}` (gauge; topic is allowlisted)
- `shadow_pipeline_circuit_breaker_state{env,region,component}` (gauge: 0 closed / 1 half-open / 2 open)
- `shadow_pipeline_circuit_breaker_open_total{env,region,component,cause}` (counter; cause is enum)

Alerts (internal pack only; tuned for dogfood):
- Page: breaker open > 10m in any region (shadow pipeline unavailable)
- Ticket: drop rate > 1% for 30m (capacity pressure)
- Ticket: scoring lag p95 > 15m for 1h (needs scaling / regression)

## Why this approach
- Keeps hard guarantees: user response is returned from control path regardless of shadow health.
- Avoids cascading failure into telemetry + storage.
- Provides clear signals for oncall: is it lag, drops, or breaker open.

## Testing
- Unit tests:
  - admission controller drop behavior + reason mapping
  - breaker state transitions (closed -> open -> half-open -> closed)
  - dedupe TTL behavior
- Integration tests (local):
  - simulated Kafka lag and downstream write errors
  - ensures router continues to serve control path while breaker open
- Load test notes: on staging, breaker prevents queue growth under forced GPU starvation; control p99 unchanged within noise (+0.2ms on router threads).

## Rollout plan
- Feature flags:
  - `shadow_pipeline_backpressure_enabled` (default: on for internal)
  - `shadow_pipeline_circuit_breaker_enabled` (default: on for internal)
- Start with internal tenants + 1 Dedicated beta tenant after SRE signoff.

## Follow-ups
- Export breaker state to Console surfaces (status pill on Shadow Experiments) (tracked in ENG-5408)
- Align external alert thresholds per Dedicated/Private defaults (PM/SRE review)

CC: @Sean Gallagher @Allison Grant (SRE/alerting), @Logan Wright @Caleb Johnson (telemetry ingestion)

Refs: ENG-5415 (backpressure/circuit breakers), incident thread: shadow scoring backlog during dogfood
commits: shadow: add AdmissionController for scoring job enqueue (semaphore + drop reasons)
shadow: implement CircuitBreaker with half-open probing + jittered timers
telemetry: emit lag/drop/breaker metrics; add allowlists for enum labels
ingest: expose kafka consumer lag proxy + downstream write error rate window
tests: breaker transition table tests + integration harness for lag simulation
ops: add default internal alert rules + runbook links
conversation: 2026-01-27 Nadia Rahman (author): This is primarily to prevent another queue runaway during dogfood. Admission controller drops shadow work first; breaker opens when lag/error exceeds thresholds. Control/user path stays untouched.

2026-01-28 Sean Gallagher: +1 on the direction. Two asks: (1) ensure breaker open does not add any synchronous dependency on Kafka lag reads in the router hot path, (2) drop reasons must be a small enum; no freeform strings.

2026-01-28 Nadia Rahman (author): Updated: breaker decisions are made in telemetry-producer async worker, not router threads. Router only checks an atomic `shadow_enabled_effective` boolean (updated every 5s). Drop reasons are now fixed enums: {capacity, dedupe, breaker_open, downstream_error}.

2026-01-29 Allison Grant: Metrics look good. Please remove `route_id` dimension from `shadow_scoring_admission_dropped_total`—we’ll blow up cardinality on high-volume tenants. Also suggest adding a `component` label to breaker state to distinguish scoring vs ingest.
2026-01-29 Nadia Rahman (author): Done. Removed route_id from all new counters; added `component={scoring,ingest}` and `cause` enum on open events.
2026-01-30 Logan Wright: For consumer lag, make sure `topic` is allowlisted, not user-provided. Also would like a doc note on how we derive lag when running in Private (no Kafka).

2026-01-30 Nadia Rahman (author): `topic` is now mapped from internal constants only. Added Private note: lag proxy is queue depth + oldest_enqueued_age in the local spool implementation; metric name stays the same, backend differs.
2026-01-31 Caleb Johnson: Can we tune half-open to start lower than 1%? If we’re truly down, 1% might still be expensive in high QPS. Suggest 0.1% and clamp max to N events/sec per region.
2026-01-31 Nadia Rahman (author): Adjusted: half-open starts at 0.1% with a hard cap of 50 events/sec/region; escalates to 1% only if lag is below 50% of threshold for 2 consecutive windows.
2026-02-01 Sean Gallagher: Please link runbook and define paging policy explicitly: page only if breaker open > 10m AND it’s during beta tenants / internal. Otherwise ticket.
2026-02-01 Nadia Rahman (author): Added `internal` alert pack only; pages route to shadow-beta oncall, ticket elsewhere. Runbook link added in alert annotations.
2026-02-02 Allison Grant: Approved. Thanks for taking the cardinality feedback quickly.
2026-02-02 Sean Gallagher: Approved. This should prevent another backlog incident.
